topic: Business breakdown: Postiz — Postiz is the ultimate agentic social media scheduler tool

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Postiz — Postiz is the ultimate agentic social media scheduler tool
pick.angle: A solo open-source founder built a free social media scheduler that has made $426K in verified revenue

research.what_it_does: An open-source, agentic social media scheduler. It schedules posts across many networks, and every plan includes an MCP server, CLI and API so AI agents like Claude or ChatGPT can post for you.
research.who_pays: Solo creators, small brands, agencies and developers or automation teams who want to schedule to many channels or let AI agents post for them. The cloud version is the paid product.
research.pricing: Official pricing page (postiz.com/pricing): Standard $29/mo, Team $39, Pro $49, Ultimate $99, each with a 7-day free trial. Annual billing works out to $23/$31/$39/$79 per month (third-party sources; not seen on the official page snippet). Channel counts are 5/10/30/100 (third-party sources). There is no permanent free hosted plan, but the code can be self-hosted free.
growth: Nevo's first instinct was SEO: he hired an Upwork freelancer for backlinks and articles, and it was useless, so he went open source instead (per a Saurav X thread summarizing his story; indiemakerlist also says the SEO-first approach failed). Source: https://x.com/saguppa/status/2038972079094038712

He open-sourced Postiz on September 1, 2024 and in his own DEV post says it grew to almost 14k GitHub stars. Source: https://dev.to/nevodavid/i-built-an-open-source-social-media-scheduling-and-it-blew-up-415e
He says he launched on Product Hunt and got #1 product of the day, week and month, with more than 2000 votes (his own DEV post).

Per a daily.dev summary of his talk, he posted launches on r/selfhosted and similar communities, where self-promotion is welcomed because the tool is free to self-host. Each launch post reportedly reached at least 200,000 views. Source: https://daily.dev/posts/the-marketing-playbook-behind-a-207k-month-saas-nevo-david-from-postiz-7w7e75jlr

Per the same summary, he stopped pitching a scheduler and sold outcomes such as going viral on TikTok or LinkedIn with automated slideshows, with Postiz mentioned only as part of the workflow. This reportedly drove 700 trials per day at peak.

He targeted a technical audience that Buffer and Sprout Social ignored: fully open source, a GitHub repo, and a dark developer-style website. He says that took Postiz to $21k MRR before the agentic wave. He then rode each wave: an n8n node, then an MCP server, then agent tooling. Source: his X article https://x.com/wickedguro/article/2090778859352563921

Trends podcast timeline: about $17K monthly revenue on New Year's Day 2026, $77K a month by April 4, and $182K in August. The founder credits selling to AI assistants for the jump. Source: https://podcast.trends.vc/episodes/this-free-scheduler-earns-326k-month-from-ai-agents/transcript

Per Mixergy, he built tools for agents like OpenClaw and simplified integrations through a CLI. Superframeworks says that when OpenClaw passed 100K GitHub stars he shipped an agent CLI, an MCP server, a ClawHub skill and programmatic landing pages. Sources: https://mixergy.com/interviews/revenue-jumped-when-he-sold-to-ai-agents/ and https://superframeworks.com/case-study/postiz

On churn, Saurav's thread says Postiz had 17% monthly churn in early 2026. It adds that he launched 'Postiz as a service', which lets people use Postiz inside their own SaaS. Source: https://x.com/saguppa/status/2038972079094038712
founder_story: Nevo David is described as a solo founder, bootstrapped with no investors, per indiemakerlist and the YouTube episode description (a third-party summary). Source: https://indiemakerlist.com/p/nevo-david/
Before Postiz he did growth at the open-source company Novu. In his own DEV post he says it grew to 31k stars in two years with his help.

Postiz started as a different product. Flownib's summary of his talk says it pivoted from a niche open-source marketing tool called GitRoom to a general social media scheduler. Buildingnow.fm says he had been consulting for open source companies and built a SaaS to help open source projects launch and earn GitHub stars.
A third-party playbook article says he openly discussed burnout after a year of working 200% while becoming a new father (secondary source: nxplace).
lessons: Pick an audience the incumbents ignore. Buffer and Sprout target marketers, so Postiz went after developers with open source, a GitHub repo and a dev-style site (his own X article).
Use open source as top-of-funnel: the free repo drew users, and the hosted cloud version is the paid product.
Coordinate launches in communities that welcome self-promotion, such as r/selfhosted, Product Hunt and GitHub trending.
Ship integrations for each new wave (n8n node, MCP server, agent CLI) so you are already there when it takes off. This is the founder's own stated approach.
Sell the outcome, not the tool. Pitching viral TikTok slideshows brought trials from people who weren't searching for schedulers.
criticism: It's a very crowded category with 'thousands of tools doing the same thing' (founder's DEV post), and there are open-source rivals like Mixpost and TryPost (openalternative.co).

The code is free to self-host under AGPL-3.0 (multiple sources), so a clone or self-hosted copy is a free substitute. The founder himself publicly asked people to build Postiz alternatives, saying the tags boost his product (X post, via trending page and Trends podcast).

A trending X page reports a former contractor leaked the codebase after being fired, and the founder threatened to sue. The same page notes the code is already public open source. This is a secondary X trending summary, so treat it with caution.
Early growth was slow and churn was high: Saurav's thread says 17% monthly churn in early 2026, and one YouTube description says it sat at $3K MRR for months.
Postiz depends on social platforms' APIs, and the hosted plan has no free tier (only a 7-day trial).
Revenue is not profit. No profit or margin data was found.
facts: Founder says Postiz was created on September 1, 2024 (DEV post). TrustMRR lists founded July 2024. Writers should use the TrustMRR date or avoid stating a founding date.
Nevo's own X article title says he took Postiz to $2M ARR.
The Trends podcast reports more than eight thousand customers on October 15 (2026) and calls Postiz a free-code app making $326,687 a month.
Trends says Nevo credits selling to AI assistants with growing Postiz more than fifteen times in eight months.
On July 2026 numbers, a secondary playbook lists 32K+ GitHub stars, about 6M downloads, and $158K MRR across 4,717 subscriptions. A $0 ad budget is claimed, but this is a secondary source.

Early 2026 timeline (nxplace and Saurav's thread): about 472 paying subscribers at about $17K MRR in November 2025 per nxplace; Docker downloaded 584K times and almost 4,000 cloud registrations at an earlier stage per Saurav.
Genviral's comparison page lists 30.6k GitHub stars and 5.6k forks. Third-party pages vary on platform count (21, 25 or 30+).
Every plan includes the MCP server, CLI, API and webhooks (official pricing page).
do_not_claim: Team size now (the founder is called 'solo' in sources, but one source mentions reinvesting in hiring and a contractor was fired)
Exact Postiz GitHub star count today (sources conflict: 25K+, 30.6k, 32K+, 34K+)
License. Most sources say AGPL-3.0, but Superframeworks says Apache 2.0. Say 'open source' only.
Founder location. TrustMRR says Hong Kong, startupbricks says Tel Aviv, so avoid it.
Annual pricing figures and per-plan channel counts as official-page facts (only confirmed via third-party pages)
That it was a 'viral' or 'SEO' success. SEO failed, and the OpenClaw 7M-view article claim comes from a secondary source (nxplace).
Exact MRR milestones from the secondary 'playbook' articles. Use the TrustMRR figures for current revenue.
That the $0 ad budget is true today: a trending page mentions a paid-ads consulting contract, and a daily.dev summary mentions paid quote-repost networks on X.
research.notes: The pricing page snippet confirms the $29, $39, $49 and $99 monthly prices and the 7-day trial. The 'Standard $29/mo' and 'Best for agencies' text appeared in the page snippet, but I did not view the live page, so check the on-screen highlight text when recording. The only other verified page is the pricing page (found via search); I did not confirm feature or gallery URLs. The best hook is that Postiz is free to self-host yet makes money, and that the founder tweeted asking people to clone it. Pricing: 'plans start at $29' matches the official page. Many third-party growth numbers are from secondary summaries of the founder's talks and posts, so attribute them ('per Nevo' or 'per a podcast') rather than stating them as fact. Mixergy's '$45K' figure is old; use TrustMRR for current numbers.
